subject: ventures/eu-battery-regulation-checker
professional: an EU product compliance manager for a battery producer or importer (e-bike packs, power banks, storage, EV packs). First checks: the Art 13 marking duties per category (collection symbol, label, QR for all batteries), the Art 77 passport and Art 11 removability dates, the Art 47 EUR 40m due-diligence test after the 2025/1561 postponement, and who is the producer for EPR (Art 3(47))

evidence.correctness: Ran the shipped compute() on 15 cases (probes.mjs in the session scratchpad; command in checks) dated 2026-11-21. Every defect the 2026-11-15 audit found in the outputs is now closed: a power bank (portable, EU manufacturer) gets qr 2027-02-18 (Art 13(6), all batteries); due diligence follows the EUR 40m turnover input (under40m=yes drops it, no/unsure keep it, 2027-08-18 per 2025/1561); nuclear-safety industrial storage stays in scope and loses exactly the Chapter III and VIII rows (collection, epr, label, qr; Art 1(6)); an EU fulfilment provider with no EU operator gets handling plus the 2019/1020 Art 4 responsible-operator row and a high finding, never 'all done'; an EU distributor gets epr-first (Art 3(47), 55(2)); on 2025-09-01 the collection symbol (Art 13(4)) already applies while the label is 'soon'. Headline dates still match: passport 2027-02-18 for LMT, industrial >2 kWh and EV; removability 2027-02-18 for portable and LMT; label 2026-08-18; conformity 2024-08-18; EPR 2025-08-18; recycled content 2028-08-18 for EV, industrial >2 kWh and SLI. 12 recomputed checks pass. Not right: an 'importer' established outside the EU is accepted and told it is 'covered' (Art 3 defines an importer as EU-established), and the portable label narrows Art 3 to 'for consumer use'. The article text could not be re-fetched this session (proxy 403 on every EU host), so the checks rest on the OJ wording the previous audit quoted.
evidence.completeness: Every feature claimed on the page and README was exercised: category, role, location and EU-operator inputs; the EUR 40m and nuclear inputs; the dated, sorted timeline; overdue/soon/pending findings; done-marking (passport and QR now have separate keys: marking passport done leaves qr open, probe 11); text summary and CSV export (tests); strict date validation (2026-02-29 rejected, 2028-02-29 accepted). The page was loaded in headless Chromium from a local server, a portable EU manufacturer checked with the button: the QR and separate-collection rows render and there are no page errors. served-copy.mjs reports no placeholder or retired origin in llms.txt, sitemap, robots or canonicals (marisstella.app itself gave a proxy 403). No stubs or TODOs. The README's 'Known gaps' honestly lists what is not built.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject root: 39/39 pass (was 29). Nine mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 8 caught, including the three that survived on 2026-11-15 (due diligence back to 2025-08-18, EPR +1 year, SLI dropped from recycled content) and new ones on QR for portable, the 40m test, the nuclear chapter list, the collection date and LMT removability. One survived: removing the `rows.length &&` guard on the 'every duty is marked done' finding (calc.mjs:149). It is equivalent today, since every in-scope role now gets at least one row, but nothing pins it if a future role or filter empties the timeline.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (182 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs and index.html. Still a pure, dependency-free obligation table with one filter, now with chapter tags so Art 1(6) is a data rule rather than a special case, and an onlyIf hook for the fulfilment fallback. The CSV export guards against formula injection. Defects: the category labels are hand-copied into index.html instead of generated from CATEGORIES (a page test checks only the option values, so label text can drift); parse() silently turns an unknown under40m/sellsEu/euOperator into a default; the importer/outside-EU contradiction is not caught. A senior JS reviewer would accept it, so 3.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, not-legal-advice, privacy and the from-memory caveat are present and asserted by page.test.mjs; 'nothing uploaded' is backed by the no-network test. The nuclear claim is fixed (the exempt option names only military/security and space, a test asserts it). The FAQ dates (passport, label, removability) match the timeline. Remaining: the portable option says 'under 5 kg, for consumer use', but Art 3(9) is 'weighs 5 kg or less, not designed specifically for industrial use', so a sealed cordless-tool pack used by tradespeople reads as not portable and the user would pick industrial-small and lose the Art 11 removability row; the LMT and EV options omit the 25 kg split (an e-motorbike pack over 25 kg is an EV battery). One wrong label text a user acts on, everything else backed: 3.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of building a per-SKU obligation calendar. For a power bank, an e-bike pack, 10 kWh storage, an EV pack, an EU distributor and an EU fulfilment house, the calendar now matches the Regulation and the findings say what is overdue; the summary and CSV are usable in a compliance file. A compliance manager would still hit, in the first hour: no weight or capacity inputs to classify the battery (the user must know the Art 3 category), no Art 12 stationary-storage safety or Art 14 state-of-health duties (both already apply), no Art 10 performance/durability, no Art 11(7) spare-part availability, no per-country EPR detail. Those are listed as known gaps. A good first read, not yet the whole job: 2.
evidence.domain: Against the Regulation and 2025/1561 as a compliance manager reads them: QR for all batteries, the EUR 40m group-consolidated turnover test, the narrow Art 1(6) nuclear carve-out by chapter, distributors as producers under Art 3(47), the separate 2025 collection-symbol date and the 'or 18 months after the implementing act' label condition are all now modelled correctly. Departures left: Art 3 category definitions paraphrased wrongly in the portable label, and Arts 10, 12, 14 and 11(7) not modelled (stated as known gaps). Within its stated limits a practitioner would sign off the timeline: 3.

defects.what: The portable category is labelled 'under 5 kg, for consumer use', but Art 3(9) defines a portable battery as sealed, 5 kg or less and not designed specifically for industrial use. A sealed cordless-tool or professional-device pack reads as not portable, so the user picks 'industrial 2 kWh or less' and loses the Art 11 removability row. The LMT and EV labels also omit the 25 kg split (an e-motorbike pack over 25 kg is an EV battery). Carried over from the 2026-11-15 audit (its low 'category labels' defect), raised to medium for the lost Art 11 row.

No weight or capacity input checks the chosen category against Art 3 (5 kg, 25 kg, 2 kWh); the user must classify the battery themselves. Carried over from 2026-11-15, still open and listed in the README's Known gaps.

Not modelled: Art 12 stationary-storage safety and Art 14 state-of-health data (both from 18 Aug 2024), Art 10 performance and durability, Art 11(7) spare-part availability, LMT recycled content from 18 Aug 2033. Carried over from 2026-11-15, listed in the README's Known gaps.

Role 'importer' with location 'outside the EU' is accepted silently and gets the importer duties and an EU-operator status of 'covered', though an importer is by definition established in the EU (Art 3). A non-EU brand that thinks of itself as the importer is never told it is the manufacturer and needs an EU importer or authorised representative.

The `rows.length &&` guard that stops 'Every duty ... is marked done' on an empty timeline (the 2026-11-15 high defect) is not pinned by any test: removing it leaves 39/39 green. It is equivalent today because every in-scope role gets at least one row.

The category and role option texts are hand-copied into index.html instead of generated from CATEGORIES and ROLES; page.test.mjs checks only the option values, so a label fix in calc.mjs can leave the page saying the old thing.

verdict: Re-audit after PRs #16236 and #16276. Eight of the ten defects filed on 2026-11-15 are closed in the code as it is now, including both highs: a power bank now gets its 18 Feb 2027 QR code, an EU fulfilment house with no EU operator is told it is the responsible operator instead of 'all done', due diligence follows the EUR 40m turnover test, nuclear-safety batteries lose only the Chapter III and VIII duties, and distributors see producer registration. 12 recomputed outputs pass; 39/39 tests pass; 8 of 9 seeded mutants are caught, including the three that survived last time. Open: the portable category label narrows Art 3(9) to consumer use (medium: a professional-tool pack loses its removability row), no weight or capacity input, Arts 10, 12, 14 and 11(7) not modelled, an out-of-EU 'importer' accepted silently, and the 'all done' guard unpinned by a test. Scores: correctness 3, completeness 3, verification 3, craft 3, claims 3, fitness 2, domain 3. Meets the bar and finished; fitness stays at 2 until the classification inputs and the Art 12/14 duties exist. The Regulation could not be re-fetched this session, so the checks rest on the OJ wording quoted in the earlier audit.
